199:                     // 1. Some common Windows commands are actually built in to cmd.exe, not executables in their own right.

202:                     // To support these situations, we have a fallback path that gets run if a command

464:     pub fn create_process(
465:         &self,
466:         stdin: Stdio,
467:         use_cmd: bool,
468:         span: Span,
469:     ) -> Result<(CommandSys, Option<PipeReader>), ShellError> {
470:         let mut process = if let Some(d) = self.env_vars.get("PWD") {
471:             let mut process = if use_cmd {
472:                 self.spawn_cmd_command(d)
473:             } else {
474:                 self.create_command(d)?
475:             };
476: 
477:             // do not try to set current directory if cwd does not exist
478:             if Path::new(&d).exists() {
479:                 process.current_dir(d);
480:             }
481:             process
482:         } else {
483:             return Err(ShellError::GenericError{
484:                 error: "Current directory not found".into(),
485:                 msg: "did not find PWD environment variable".into(),
486:                 span: Some(span),
487:                 help: Some(concat!(
488:                     "The environment variable 'PWD' was not found. ",
489:                     "It is required to define the current directory when running an external command."
490:                 ).into()),
491:                 inner:Vec::new(),
492:             });
493:         };
494: 
495:         process.envs(&self.env_vars);
496: 
497:         // If the external is not the last command, its output will get piped
498:         // either as a string or binary
499:         let reader = if matches!(self.out, OutDest::Pipe) && matches!(self.err, OutDest::Pipe) {
500:             let (reader, writer) = os_pipe::pipe()?;
501:             let writer_clone = writer.try_clone()?;
502:             process.stdout(writer);
503:             process.stderr(writer_clone);
504:             Some(reader)
505:         } else {
506:             process.stdout(Stdio::try_from(&self.out)?);
507:             process.stderr(Stdio::try_from(&self.err)?);
508:             None
509:         };
510: 
511:         process.stdin(stdin);
512: 
513:         Ok((process, reader))
514:     }

516:     fn create_command(&self, cwd: &str) -> Result<CommandSys, ShellError> {
517:         // in all the other cases shell out
518:         if cfg!(windows) {
519:             //TODO. This should be modifiable from the config file.
520:             // We could give the option to call from powershell
521:             // for minimal builds cwd is unused
522:             if self.name.item.ends_with(".cmd") || self.name.item.ends_with(".bat") {
523:                 Ok(self.spawn_cmd_command(cwd))
524:             } else {
525:                 self.spawn_simple_command(cwd)
526:             }
527:         } else {
528:             self.spawn_simple_command(cwd)
529:         }
530:     }

532:     /// Spawn a command without shelling out to an external shell
533:     pub fn spawn_simple_command(&self, cwd: &str) -> Result<std::process::Command, ShellError> {
534:         let (head, _, _) = trim_enclosing_quotes(&self.name.item);
535:         let head = nu_path::expand_to_real_path(head)
536:             .to_string_lossy()
537:             .to_string();
538: 
539:         let mut process = std::process::Command::new(head);
540: 
541:         for (arg, arg_keep_raw) in self.args.iter().zip(self.arg_keep_raw.iter()) {
542:             trim_expand_and_apply_arg(&mut process, arg, arg_keep_raw, cwd);
543:         }
544: 
545:         Ok(process)
546:     }

548:     /// Spawn a cmd command with `cmd /c args...`
549:     pub fn spawn_cmd_command(&self, cwd: &str) -> std::process::Command {
550:         let mut process = std::process::Command::new("cmd");
551: 
552:         // Disable AutoRun
553:         // TODO: There should be a config option to enable/disable this
554:         // Alternatively (even better) a config option to specify all the arguments to pass to cmd
555:         process.arg("/D");
556: 
557:         process.arg("/c");
558:         process.arg(&self.name.item);
559:         for (arg, arg_keep_raw) in self.args.iter().zip(self.arg_keep_raw.iter()) {
560:             // https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1200235/how-to-pass-a-quoted-pipe-character-to-cmd-exe
561:             // cmd.exe needs to have a caret to escape a pipe
562:             let arg = Spanned {
563:                 item: arg.item.replace('|', "^|"),
564:                 span: arg.span,
565:             };
566: 
567:             trim_expand_and_apply_arg(&mut process, &arg, arg_keep_raw, cwd)
568:         }
569: 
570:         process
571:     }
572: }

574: fn trim_expand_and_apply_arg(
575:     process: &mut CommandSys,
576:     arg: &Spanned<String>,
577:     arg_keep_raw: &bool,
578:     cwd: &str,
579: ) {
580:     // if arg is quoted, like "aa", 'aa', `aa`, or:
581:     // if arg is a variable or String interpolation, like: $variable_name, $"($variable_name)"
582:     // `as_a_whole` will be true, so nu won't remove the inner quotes.
583:     let (trimmed_args, mut run_glob_expansion, mut keep_raw) = trim_enclosing_quotes(&arg.item);
584:     if *arg_keep_raw {
585:         keep_raw = true;
586:         // it's a list or a variable, don't run glob expansion either
587:         run_glob_expansion = false;
588:     }
589:     let mut arg = Spanned {
590:         item: if keep_raw {
591:             trimmed_args
592:         } else {
593:             remove_quotes(trimmed_args)
594:         },
595:         span: arg.span,
596:     };
597:     if !keep_raw {
598:         arg.item = nu_path::expand_tilde(arg.item)
599:             .to_string_lossy()
600:             .to_string();
601:     }
602:     let cwd = PathBuf::from(cwd);
603:     if arg.item.contains('*') && run_glob_expansion {
604:         // we need to run glob expansion, so it's NeedExpand.
605:         let path = Spanned {
606:             item: NuGlob::Expand(arg.item.clone()),
607:             span: arg.span,
608:         };
609:         if let Ok((prefix, matches)) = nu_engine::glob_from(&path, &cwd, arg.span, None) {
610:             let matches: Vec<_> = matches.collect();
611: 
612:             // FIXME: do we want to special-case this further? We might accidentally expand when they don't
613:             // intend to
614:             if matches.is_empty() {
615:                 process.arg(&arg.item);
616:             }
617:             for m in matches {
618:                 if let Ok(arg) = m {
619:                     let arg = if let Some(prefix) = &prefix {
620:                         if let Ok(remainder) = arg.strip_prefix(prefix) {
621:                             let new_prefix = if let Some(pfx) = diff_paths(prefix, &cwd) {
622:                                 pfx
623:                             } else {
624:                                 prefix.to_path_buf()
625:                             };
626: 
627:                             new_prefix.join(remainder).to_string_lossy().to_string()
628:                         } else {
629:                             arg.to_string_lossy().to_string()
630:                         }
631:                     } else {
632:                         arg.to_string_lossy().to_string()
633:                     };
634: 
635:                     process.arg(&arg);
636:                 } else {
637:                     process.arg(&arg.item);
638:                 }
639:             }
640:         }
641:     } else {
642:         process.arg(&arg.item);
643:     }
644: }

646: /// Given an invalid command name, try to suggest an alternative
647: fn suggest_command(attempted_command: &str, engine_state: &EngineState) -> Option<String> {
648:     let commands = engine_state.get_signatures(false);
649:     let command_folded_case = attempted_command.to_folded_case();
650:     let search_term_match = commands.iter().find(|sig| {
651:         sig.search_terms
652:             .iter()
653:             .any(|term| term.to_folded_case() == command_folded_case)
654:     });
655:     match search_term_match {
656:         Some(sig) => Some(sig.name.clone()),
657:         None => {
658:             let command_names: Vec<String> = commands.iter().map(|sig| sig.name.clone()).collect();
659:             did_you_mean(&command_names, attempted_command)
660:         }
661:     }
662: }

664: /// This function returns a tuple with 3 items:
665: /// 1st item: trimmed string.
666: /// 2nd item: a boolean value indicate if it's ok to run glob expansion.
667: /// 3rd item: a boolean value indicate if we need to keep raw string.
668: fn trim_enclosing_quotes(input: &str) -> (String, bool, bool) {
669:     let mut chars = input.chars();
670: 
671:     match (chars.next(), chars.next_back()) {
672:         (Some('"'), Some('"')) => (chars.collect(), false, true),
673:         (Some('\''), Some('\'')) => (chars.collect(), false, true),
674:         // We treat back-quoted strings as bare words, so there's no need to keep them as raw strings
675:         (Some('`'), Some('`')) => (chars.collect(), true, false),
676:         _ => (input.to_string(), true, false),
677:     }
678: }
679: 
680: fn remove_quotes(input: String) -> String {
681:     let mut chars = input.chars();
682: 
683:     match (chars.next_back(), input.contains('=')) {
684:         (Some('"'), true) => chars
685:             .collect::<String>()
686:             .replacen('"', "", 1)
687:             .replace(r#"\""#, "\""),
688:         (Some('\''), true) => chars.collect::<String>().replacen('\'', "", 1),
689:         _ => input,
690:     }
691: }

693: fn extract_stdio(pipeline: PipelineData) -> (PipelineData, Stdio) {
694:     match pipeline {
695:         PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, metadata) => match stream.into_stdio() {
696:             Ok(pipe) => (PipelineData::Empty, pipe),
697:             Err(stream) => (PipelineData::ByteStream(stream, metadata), Stdio::piped()),
698:         },
699:         PipelineData::Empty => (PipelineData::Empty, Stdio::inherit()),
700:         data => (data, Stdio::piped()),
701:     }
702: }
